 LIVE COVERAGE: President Trump visiting Wichita area today for midterm rally 
 POTUS coming to Park City’s Heartland Credit Union Arena to rally Kansas Republicans 
 By Matt Heilman Published : Oct. 19, 2026 at 6:04 AM CDT | Updated : 1 hour ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google WICHITA, Kan. (KWCH) - Monday brings President Donald Trump’s first visit to the Wichita area in a decade. The president is expected to address a crowd Monday evening at Park City’s Heartland Credit Union Arena, an approximately 6,500-seat venue off 77th Street North, between Broadway and Interstate 135, in Park City.
 Monday’s presidential appearance follows through on Trump’s promise for a “Kansas Style Rally” in support of Senator Roger Marshall .
 The event features a program starting at 4:30 p.m., with the president expected to speak at 6 p.m. Doors open to the public at 2:30 p.m. Vehicles began lining up Sunday night. 
 The link for guests to acquire tickets has been updated to:  https://events.gop.com/events/midterm-rally-in-park-city-kansas-president-donald-j-trump-ks 
 Trump supporter Jason Waters was among the first in line. 
 “I came earlier to scout out the place and decided, ‘Well, maybe I should come now,” Waters told 12 News on Sunday night. “So, here I am, eight to 10 cars in line and I’m not leaving.” 
 The line grew substantially overnight, with several toward the front of the line setting up tents on Sunday. 
 Early Monday morning, one Trump supporter in line said he drove about two hours for the rally in Park City and was looking forward to fellowship surrounding the event. 
 “What am I hoping to see? You know, the camaraderie from the crowd, the love from the crowd,” he said. “It’s a feeling that’s hard to get anywhere else these days.” 
 The Trump supporter said he previously drove 13 hours to see the president. 
 What to know if you go: 
 For those attending Monday’s rally in Park City, Heartland Credit Union Arena has a clear bag policy and bags cannot be larger than 14 by six inches. 
 You can bring in a small clutch or purse, but those can’t be larger than five-and-a-half by eight-and-a-half inches. 
 You cannot bring strollers, car seats, weapons of any kind or any outside food or drinks. Those planning to attend are encouraged to arrive early and have your ticket ready to go, either pulled up on your device or printed off. 
 Traffic and Parking: 
 Street closures for Monday’s rally include Broadway between 77th and 85th Streets North from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. 
 Briar Rose Lane and the southern portion of Arena Drive will also be closed. 
 As for parking, those parking at the arena should take Arena Drive from 85th Street. There will also be overflow parking across the highway at Gilley’s, with buses shuttling people between Gilley’s and the arena. Those planning to use a rideshare like Uber or Lyft should arrange to be dropped off at Gilley’s.
